title: split-terraform-state-for-ephemeral-network-resources-and-zero-downtime-migrations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our current monolithic Terraform state for networking (VPCs, subnets, NAT/EIP allocations, and ephemeral infra) makes small network changes expensive, increases chance of destructive plans, and slows CI/CD plans. Several recent outages were exacerbated as rollbacks required unpinned provider upgrades and manual state surgery. Goal: Decompose the existing networking state into logical, environment-scoped backends that isolate ephemeral resources (test clusters, ephemeral NATs, CI workspaces) from long-lived primitives (VPCs, peering, transit gateways). This will reduce plan/apply times, enable safe parallel changes, and support rolling migrations with zero-downtime cutovers for runtime services. Scope: - Introduce new Terraform backends and state buckets keyed by: region / env / resource-class - Extract ephemeral resources into a separate module and remote state bucket with short lifecycle and TTL - Rework module inputs to avoid cross-module implicit dependencies; use explicit remote_state data where necessary - Add a migration controller script to perform state mv operations and verify resource bindings - Upgrade AWS provider from 4.x to 5.x in the networking modules (followed by verification) Non-goals: - Full multi-cloud refactor (we will keep AWS first) - Large application infra refactors or service-level deployments Success criteria: - Average terraform plan time for networking changes reduced by >=40% in CI - No customer-facing network interruptions during staged migration (verified by smoke tests) - All new envs use decomposed backends by default - Rollback plan tested and validated in staging Migration approach: 1) Prepare new backend buckets per region with ACLs and lifecycle policies 2) Convert a single non-critical environment (staging-us-west-2) by moving state for ephemeral resources into new backend using terraform state mv and import where needed 3) Run full CI plan compare and automated smoke tests (connectivity, NAT egress, subnet tagging) 4) Promote learnings and automate state move for additional envs in waves 5) After ephemeral split is stable, migrate long-lived primitives using canary day windows Rollback strategy: Keep snapshots and retain sources of truth in previous backends for 30 days. If migration causes regression, run inverse terraform moves to restore original state. Observability & validation: - Add per-backend terraform plan duration metrics to telemetry - Add drift detection checks for split state boundaries - Post-migration runbook with checklist and automated smoke-run logs Risks & mitigations: - Risk: state move could orphan resources if references are missed. Mitigation: pre-flight linter to detect implicit references and manual review step. - Risk: provider upgrade induces breaking changes. Mitigation: pin upgrade to single module at a time, run downstream tests in a forked account. - Risk: IAM misconfiguration on new buckets. Mitigation: bootstrap script will validate bucket IAM, KMS/CMK bindings, and encryption before migration
acceptance_criteria: New remote backends provisioned for region/env/resource-class with encryption and lifecycle policies
Ephemeral resources state moved for staging-us-west-2 with no plan drift and CI plan times reduced >=40%
Automated smoke tests (connectivity, NAT egress, routing, tagging) pass post-migration
Terraform AWS provider upgrade applied to networking modules with documented compatibility notes
Rollback procedure documented and tested in staging with state snapshots available
